newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASX queries BHP on disclosure timing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASX queries BHP on disclosure timing.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) on Thursday released correspondence with The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) in which it raised concerns about BHP's timing of an information release concerning an oil flow at a BHP well.

In a letter dated October 16, the ASX queried the thouroughness of weekly drilling reports released by BHP on October 3 and October 10 which indicated that the Buffalo-1 exploration well offshore Western Australia was "being prepared to be plugged and abandoned" and was "plugged and abandoned".
BHP then announced on October 14 that Buffalo-1 had flowed oil at the rate of 11,790 barrels per day.
"It appears the company may have had disclosure obligations under listing rule 5.4 immediately the stem test results for Buffalo-1 were known," the ASX said in its October 16 letter.
Listing rule 5.4 covers disclosure requirements for mining and oil companies.
In a response to the letter on October 17, BHP said it believed its release of information was in the best interest of the company and its shareholders.
BHP also said that as it was listed as an industrial company, it was not required to comply with the special reporting requirements set out in listing rule 5.4.

The ASX's responded to this letter on the same day and said it knew of no reason for the belief that ASX was aware that BHP was proceeding on the basis that it was not required to comply with rules regulating mining and oil companies. It said it expected BHP to make disclosures under these rules.
